name: compose: call a library item per part

slots.name: PARTS
slots.doc: the parts to hand to the child: [{key, input}]

slots.name: REF
slots.doc: the child's library hash, a literal (MUTABLE_TARGET otherwise)

slots.name: ON_REFUSE
slots.doc: value: a refused part comes back as {refused} and is flagged

slots.name: ARG
slots.doc: what every part input is; must be accepted by the child's contract.input (CALL_TYPE)

slots.name: READS
slots.doc: what COMBINE reads of a child output; must be implied by the child's contract.output (CALL_TYPE)

when.instructions: Does the task contain several parts that each need the same sub-job, and does the library hold an item that does that sub-job?
How do the parts relate to the library item?

criteria.same-shape: each part is the item's input as it stands
criteria.adapt: each part needs a pure reshaping first
criteria.partial: the item covers only some parts

checklist.text: The call target is a literal hash.
What is passed meets the child's input contract; what is read is in its output contract.
Child budgets times concurrency stay below the parent's.
A child that may see inputs outside its profile needs a fallback.
Children are pure; effects run once, in the parent's envelope.
No path calls back into an ancestor.

companions.why: a quorum over the parts that came back

slots.PARTS: (task, x) => x.entities.map(e => ({ key: e.code, input: { entity: e.code, lines: e.lines } }))
slots.COMBINE: (kids, parts) => ({ entities: parts.map((p, i) => kids[i].refused || kids[i].deopt ? { entity: p.key, review: kids[i].refused || kids[i].deopt.kind } : { entity: p.key, totalMinor: kids[i].totalMinor }), totalMinor: kids.reduce((n, k) => n + (k.totalMinor || 0), 0) })
